s13.title: 118 Robonauts | Behind the Bumpers | 2025 FRC REEFSCAPE Robot

bet.text: The robot should never wait for a game piece to reach the scoring mechanism. The binder lists this first among its architecture goals.

demand.text: Qualifications: maximize ranking points by scoring more coral and algae, leaving time in auto to push partners off the line, minimizing coral cycle time, scoring in the opposing processor for Coopertition, and climbing a deep cage. Eliminations: maximize alliance score.

auto.text: Auto sequences are scripted in Lua. Algae autos were developed on April 10 and a four-piece coral auto on April 12, before the championship.
The robot lines up on a station tag, always at the same slot, so autos could be sped up without worry about slipping.

cycle.text: The coral intake takes coral in any orientation and hands it to the end effector. The goal was a direct handoff with no staging.
The driver holds a button once a reef tag is in view. The robot lines up, raises and places; release is automatic or one button press.

endgame.text: Rollers with embedded magnets pull the cage into two one-way latches. Limit switches confirm both latches, and a Spectra winch lifts the robot.
The binder gives less than 2 seconds for the automatic climb; an interviewed member says about 3 seconds.

fallback.text: An architecture goal was to keep the most functions if one mechanism is lost in a match.
A button pad is kept for peripheral and backup controls.

gave_up.text: The algae floor intake was first used heavily at the championship, partly because its handoff sequence took a long time to dial in.
The silver robot, the first of three built, was originally 8 pounds overweight, and the team chased small weight savings all season (a thread reply that reads as the team's).

changed.text: A re-orienting belt joined the coral intake after the reveal, because drivers struggled with perpendicular coral. The first climb had side fingers and was mostly driver operated; intake wheels, limit switches, magnets and software sped it up.
On March 26 both robots swapped from L2+ to L1+ gearing.

outcome.text: 110-12-0 in official play; won the Milstein division; captain of the Milstein alliance on Einstein; ranked 12 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 105.38, Milstein).

facts.text: SDS MK4-C modules at L1+, Kraken X60 propulsion and Kraken X44 steering, on a 29 x 29 in frame
Garolite spacers lower the frame by 3/4 in
Custom hubs in Grip Lock wheels eliminate tire flex
Kraken shafts are cut down to eliminate spacers, saving about 1/2 lb across the robot

cost.text: Hubs printed in Onyx had their bearing holes wallow out after the first event, stock hubs ran at the second with noticeably lower accuracy, and a new print in PA6-CF20 lasted the season (a thread reply that reads as the team's)

facts.text: One Kraken X44, SDS bearing blocks, 0.040 in wall 1 x 2 in MAXTube
Constant force springs off-load it
A vernier scale system tensions the arm and elevator belts
An interviewed member says it stays down for stages one to three and moves only for stage four
No upper hard stop was designed; the belt clamps meeting the constant force springs act as one (a thread reply that reads as the team's)

functions.name: Arm

solves.text: Keep the center of gravity low

functions.type: pivoting arm on the elevator carriage

facts.text: One Kraken X44 drives the pivot through two custom cycloidal gearboxes
The arm reduction is about 50 to 1
Pivot, coral and algae motors sit in the base of the carriage, and belts run through the box tube to the end effector

solves.text: Be more compact and lighter than bought planetary gearboxes

facts.text: 23:1 reduction, used twice on the arm pivot and once on the coral intake pivot
Backlash, about
Two offset discs in heat-treated 4140 steel reduce vibration; steel tubes roll on dowel pins
Designed in the 2024 off-season

functions.name: Coral Intake

solves.text: Collect coral in any orientation and keep control of it through the handoff

functions.type: floor roller intake with re-orienting belt

facts.text: A sideways re-orienting belt takes coral in any orientation; perpendicular coral is knocked sideways
One Kraken X60 and one Kraken X44 drive the rollers; a Kraken X44 drives the pivot through a 23:1 cycloidal
Two roller motors let the coral stop in the intake, to be scored in L1 or handed off
For L1 the two sides spin opposite ways, which the team calls hot dog position
Bent and twisted belts drive off-axis shafts from motors in the chassis
Rollers are pool noodle and custom TPU covered in silicone tubing

solves.text: Take algae from the floor in a small space that the climb also passes through

facts.text: One Kraken X44 drives the rollers and one drives the pivot
Custom 3D printed 15T bevel gears have reinforced teeth
The algae wedges into two prints, and a print on the climb ramps it into the end effector
Roller current and a sensor show where the algae is, so the sequence can step without dropping it

cost.text: The jackshaft had to be split in three to fit around the climb
The automated handoff took a long time to dial in

functions.name: End-Effector

solves.text: Add compliance while placing coral on L4

functions.type: internal coral gripper with algae rollers

facts.text: It grips the inside of the coral, from the floor intake or the human player station
It takes algae from the reef and the floor intake, and scores in the processor and barge
Mostly polycarbonate, to save weight and resist impact
X belts let material be cut away so the coral can tip over an L4 branch
The algae side is wide, with cone wheels in grip tape, geared for three times the coral side's torque
Two springs react on the bar of the barge, so the wheels dunk the algae over
Two drives pass through a 2 in gap by splitting the shaft in the middle

functions.name: Climb

solves.text: Capture a swinging cage with the driver only driving straight into it

functions.type: winched cage intake with one-way latches

facts.text: Kraken X44 at 33.6:1, shared by deploy and final rotation; a Spectra winch rotates the cage intake
Torsion springs deploy it
Custom TPU rollers with embedded rare-earth magnets pull the cage into two one-way latches
Magnets at the back add resistance so the cage does not swing back, and magnets in the lower wheels catch a swinging cage
After the first limit switch the wheels reverse, to torque the cage into the top latch
An 18-channel CAN node gives a star topology, one channel per device or subsystem
A power board feeds low-current devices, with six switchable channels, protection and status LEDs
Single devices can be power cycled

solves.text: Let a single driver run sequences that took a driver and an operator before

facts.text: Two Limelight 4s automate coral scoring
They face the reef about 6 or 7 in from robot center, so one is centered on the tag when scoring on a branch
Branch positions are measured during field calibration and the offsets go into code
A CANrange measures barge distance for net scoring
Current in the end effector wheels shows that the coral is held

decisions.choice: Coral intake delivers directly to the end effector
decisions.because: an integration goal was no staging of the piece for the handoff

decisions.choice: Avoid passing game pieces through the lift
decisions.because: it was one of the binder's system integration goals

decisions.choice: Motors low in the chassis and carriage
decisions.because: it keeps the center of gravity low
many sequences are automated and easy to run from one controller
tire flex is amplified at L4 height and lowers automated scoring accuracy (a thread reply that reads as the team's)

decisions.choice: Change the algae end effector roller ratio from 5.6:1 to 15:1
decisions.because: the handoff largely set the geometry, and it cut calculated stall current from 35 A to 13 A, though the writer thinks 15 or 20 A was run (a thread reply that reads as the team's)

decisions.choice: Shortened Kraken shafts on the swerve modules
decisions.because: removing 1/2 in spacers gave most of the weight saving, and a mount without small spacers slightly improves cooling (a thread reply that reads as the team's)
they are lighter, have fewer parts and take less width (a thread reply that reads as the team's)
decisions.cost: motor shafts interfere with the steering pulley and drive gears unless spaced or shortened

decisions.choice: About 1 pound of weight margin kept all season
decisions.because: there was then always weight to solve problems with (a thread reply that reads as the team's)
